title: Waiting for Lefty by Clifford Odets at Classic Stage Company #waiting...
transcript: Leave it to Steven Pasquale to turn a 36-page script into a sweeping tableau with music and movement, in his directorial debut. Waiting for Lefty is set at a union meeting during The Great Depression, where workers are floating a strike against poor wages, among other things. Isn't it a little odd to be producing this play in New York right now, where the average household income of a Broadway attendee is over $250,000? I think it's a fair question, but this play does present a lot of grievances beyond class struggles. Through a series of vignettes that highlight the economic strain that these workers are facing, we also acknowledge the rat race from capitalism constantly moving the goal posts, the myth of meritocracy, corporate greed, and workplace discrimination. Adam Kantor as a radicalized doctor and Tala Ashe as a financially suffocated housewife are especially memorable, as are the live musical numbers. The dream-like movement and cinematic direction give the piece a timeless quality, and I connected with it more than I expected to. Aside from the occasionally misplaced interpretive dance moment and the crowd sound effects which cut in like a cheap laugh track, this is a pretty successful exercise in elevating an otherwise cold and distant piece.
